tagline: Institutional governance and internal control assurance through comprehensive audit and advisory services
hero_kpi_rationale: The audit completion rate of 56% reflects the actual operational capacity of the department, impacted by unplanned additional audits on executive spending compliance, thereby revealing institutional governance priorities.

kpis.name: Audit Completion Rate
kpis.explanation: Percentage of planned audits that were completed during the year.
kpis.description: The low rate is due to unplanned additional audits on senior executive spending, compensation, travel and entertainment expenses, as well as Chancellor's Administrative Fund expenses and University House fees.
kpis.signal: Only 56% of planned audits completed due to unforeseen additional audits.

kpis.name: Audit Hours
kpis.explanation: Total number of hours dedicated to audit projects.
kpis.description: Additional audits covered senior executive compensation, travel and entertainment expenses, as well as Chancellor's Administrative Fund expenses and University House fees.
kpis.signal: 2,087 additional hours versus plan due to mandatory additional audits.

kpis.name: Advisory Hours
kpis.explanation: Hours dedicated to advisory services and consultations.
kpis.description: Resources were redirected to mandatory audits due to workload overages from priority activities. A total of 1,445 hours were planned but only 733 hours were devoted to advisory services.
kpis.signal: Less than half of planned advisory hours utilized.

kpis.name: Investigation Hours
kpis.explanation: Time spent on investigations related to allegations of misconduct.
kpis.description: Investigations are managed by an internal task force under whistleblower policy. Seven new investigations were initiated in FY 2006, all following irregularity reports, with four related to misuse of university resources.
kpis.signal: 40% of hours devoted to one major investigation in the public affairs office.

kpis.name: Net Available Hours
kpis.explanation: Total hours available after deduction of uncontrollable time.
kpis.description: Includes permanent staff hours and adjusts for administrative time. Based on 7.0 FTE with deduction of 2,246 uncontrollable hours to yield a net total of 12,789 available hours.
kpis.signal: Total operational capacity measured in available hours.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of 18.16 billion € in the most recent year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of 2.25 billion € in the most recent year

kpis.name: Cash & Equivalents
kpis.description: Cash & equivalents extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Cash & equivalents of 2.25 billion € in the most recent year

risks.title: Systemic failures in employee separation management
risks.score_rationale: Risk classified as 'high risk' and 'past due' in the A&AS FY2006 report (Audit #469); strong language ('failure', 'overpayments', repeated extensions); persistent trend with 2 MCAs still open at fiscal year-end; core operational category for a public institution of this size.

risks.title: Critical dependency on key payroll personnel
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned as direct cause of two MCA deadline extensions on high-risk items ('key resignations', 'absence of a Payroll Office Manager', 'resignation of the primary IT specialist'); direct causal language; concerning trend across the fiscal year; documented operational impact.

risks.title: Insufficient internal audit human resources
risks.score_rationale: Reported in the Staffing section: only 6 positions filled out of 6.85; 4 planned audits not started at fiscal year-end; moderate language but concrete impact on risk coverage; stable trend with structural understaffing.

risks.title: Student and administrative data security risks
risks.score_rationale: Specific advisory project on data security (Graduate Division Data Security, Appendix B) was initiated in FY2006; presence of only one IT specialist within the audit team underscores vulnerability; emerging trend in the university context; high reputational impact category.

risks.title: Insufficient control of travel and entertainment expenses
risks.score_rationale: Six distinct audits on Vice-Chancellor travel and entertainment expenses were issued in FY2006 (Audits 478A through 478G); multiplicity of concerned entities indicates systemic risk; recurring compliance language; stable trend with UC policy non-compliance risk.

risks.title: Financial systems and consolidated billing integrity
risks.score_rationale: Audit #469 (Consolidated Billings) is the sole audit generating two high-risk MCAs still open; Berkeley Financial System Vendoring (Audit #475) was also audited; high-risk language; concerning trend with failing account reconciliations.

risks.title: Ethics and misuse of university resources risks
risks.score_rationale: Five formal investigations completed in FY2006 (including Athletics Financial Aid, Cal Dance Team, Economics); dedicated audit on ethics policies (Audit #471); presence of Locally Designated Official for investigations; stable but recurring trend across multiple units.
